message.reasoning_content:
The user wants a block-breaking game (Breakout/Arkanoid). Let me build a rich, polished single-file HTML game with canvas. Key design instincts: - For a game, the game itself should be the opening — the most characteristic thing to lead with. So the canvas is front and center, framed like an arcade cabinet, with a distinctive HUD. - Pair a display face with a readable body face. For arcade: maybe a chunky display face. Let's use something like "Bungee" or "Chakra Petch" for display and "IBM Plex Sans" / "Space Grotesk" for body. Japanese text needed since request is Japanese. So Japanese-capable fonts. Google Fonts: "Dela Gothic One" (display, Japanese+Latin), body: "Zen Kaku Gothic New" or "IBM Plex Sans JP". Dela Gothic One is bold and arcade-ish. Or "Bungee" for Latin numerals in HUD plus "Zen Kaku Gothic New" for Japanese body. Let's do: display = "Dela Gothic One" (very characteristic, chunky), body = "Zen Kaku Gothic New" (readable Japanese). And maybe "Bungee" for score numerals. Keep to 2-3 families. Palette: an arcade cabinet feels right in deep teal/ink with warm amber/coral accents — retro CRT but not literally a black screen with one neon glow. Let's do a layered background: deep ink-blue/teal with a subtle scanline + dot grid + soft radial glows in amber and cyan, plus a cabinet frame in warm off-white? Hmm. Let me design: background = deep "sumi" navy #0d1b2a-ish with layered gradients, plus a faint grid, plus drifting light. Cabinet frame in a warm sand/graphite. Accent colors: hot coral #ff5a5f, amber #ffb347, mint #4ecdc4, electric cyan. Blocks in a warm rainbow ramp (coral→amber→lime→cyan). Paddle in cream. Ball glowing white-amber. Game features (rich, alive): - Canvas breakout with multiple levels, block types: normal, tough (2 hits), steel (indestructible), and power-up drops: expand paddle, multiball, slow ball, laser? extra life. - Particles on block break, screen shake, ball trail, paddle glow. - Combo counter, score multiplier, floating score text. - Levels with patterns. - HUD: score, lives, level, combo, high score (localStorage). - Start overlay, level-clear overlay, game over overlay, pause. - Mouse + touch + keyboard controls. - Sound via WebAudio (blips) with mute toggle. - Side panel: controls legend, power-up legend, level list. - Micro-interactions: buttons with hover, scanline overlay, CRT vignette. - Scroll reveals for a section below explaining power-ups? Maybe keep it mostly one screen but add a compact "how to play" panel. Layout: asymmetric — left rail with vertical title + stats, center canvas, right rail with legend. On mobile stack. Let me write the code carefully. Canvas: logical size 900x640? Use responsive scaling with devicePixelRatio. Let's do logical W=880, H=620. Game architecture: - state: 'ready' | 'playing' | 'paused' | 'levelclear' | 'gameover' | 'win' - paddle: x, w, h - balls: array {x,y,vx,vy,r, speed} - bricks: array {x,y,w,h,hp,type,color} - powerups falling - particles - floaters (score text) - lasers maybe skip; add laser for fun? Keep: expand, multiball, slow, life, laser (paddle shoots). Laser adds complexity but fun. I'll include laser: press Space or auto-fire while holding? Let's do: laser powerup gives 8 seconds of auto-fire every 300ms. Space fires manually. Hmm, Space also launches ball. Let's have ball auto-launch on click/space; laser auto-fires. Simpler: powerups = expand, multi, slow, laser, life, and a bad one: shrink? Let's include shrink as a hazard (dark block drops). Actually keep positive-heavy: expand, multi, slow, laser, life. Plus a rare "shield" (one-time ball save at bottom). Shield is nice. Bricks types: normal (1hp), tough (2hp, cracked look), steel (∞, only destroyed by... nothing; just indestructible), gold (bonus points, drops more). Levels: define patterns as string arrays. Let me define level layouts with characters: - '.' empty - '1' normal - '2' tough - '3' steel - '5' gold Colors by row or by type. I'll color by type with hue variation per row. Level patterns (10 wide grid maybe). Let's use cols=11, brick width computed. Let me write 5 levels + a final. Level 1: simple rows ``` ........... .111111111. .111111111. .111111111. ``` Better to make interesting shapes. L1: ``` ........... .111111111. .111111111. ..1111111.. ``` L2: ``` ..2.....2.. .111...111. .112121211. ..1111111.. .....3..... ``` Hmm keep it readable. I'll craft 6 levels. Physics: ball-paddle collision with angle based on hit offset. Speed increases slightly over time / per level. Max speed cap. Sub-stepping for collision to avoid tunneling: move in steps of at most r/2. Brick collision: find overlapping brick, determine side by penetration depth. Powerup drop chance ~14%. Screen shake: offset canvas translate. Trail: store last positions. Rendering: nice gradients, glow via shadowBlur (careful perf, fine). Background inside canvas: dark navy with subtle grid + faint horizontal glow lines. Overlays: HTML overlays on top of canvas with backdrop blur — but I don't want blur everywhere. Use solid panels with strong borders. Let me also add a "cabinet" look: outer frame with rounded corners on the canvas area only, thick border, corner bolts, marquee at top with title in Dela Gothic One. Header: marquee bar with title "BLOCK CRUSHER" / Japanese "ブロック崩し" and a small animated strip of colored blocks. Left rail: SCORE big numerals, LEVEL, LIVES (as block icons), COMBO meter, HIGH SCORE. Right rail: POWER-UP legend with colored chips, CONTROLS, and mute/pause buttons. Below: a section with level gallery? Maybe a "LEVELS" strip showing mini previews with scroll reveal. That adds richness. Let's add a bottom section: "LEVEL DATA" with mini grids rendered from the same patterns via JS, revealing on scroll. Nice. Also a stats line: total blocks, etc. Let me write it. Fonts: ``` ``` Dela Gothic One for display (Japanese + Latin), Bungee for numerals/HUD, Zen Kaku Gothic New for body. Three families — display + numeric accent + body. Fine. Colors: - ink: #0a1420 - deep: #0f1e2e - panel: #14283c - cream: #f4efe6 - coral: #ff5f56 - amber: #ffb020 - mint: #38d9a9 - cyan: #35b8e0 - violet? avoid violet. Use lime #a3e635? ok sparingly. Background page: layered — base #0a1420, radial glows amber top-left low opacity, cyan bottom-right, plus repeating-linear-gradient scanlines very subtle, plus a dot grid.
